overall_summary: The candidate gave specific examples of improving latency with caching and described idempotent webhook handling with enough detail to assess ownership. Trade-offs around splitting a monolith were pragmatic. Depth on streaming systems was thinner than the JD emphasized.
strengths: Concrete metrics when discussing caching impact on tail latency
Clear mental model for idempotency in payment webhooks
Honest about Kafka experience being limited rather than overstating
gaps: Less demonstrated depth on high-throughput streaming and consumer semantics
Kubernetes operations mostly described at deploy/service level
scenario_handling_notes: Silence was handled with a short check-in without solution hints. Clarification narrowed the question scope. Off-topic drift was redirected once and the candidate refocused.

competencies.summary: Solid articulation of idempotent APIs and collaboration patterns; good alignment with role responsibilities.

evidence.quote: We used idempotency keys on the webhook handler so retries from the processor would not double-charge.
After we cached the hottest read paths in Redis, p95 for the listing endpoint dropped roughly forty percent.

competencies.summary: Understands where queues help but limited hands-on detail on delivery guarantees and operational failure modes.

evidence.quote: I have not run Kafka in production myself — most of my async work has been Redis-backed workers and scheduled jobs.
